en.name: Prosciutto
en.summary: Prosciutto is Italian dry-cured ham: a pork leg salted and air-dried for a year or more, then sliced paper-thin and eaten raw. Refrigerated at 4 °C (40 °F) or below it keeps 2–3 months, and it freezes for 1 month. It is the reference point other dry-cured whole muscles on this site are measured against.
en.pantry: Sliced or vacuum-packed prosciutto is a chilled product, not a cupboard one. A whole leg is a different object — dry, salty and protected on its outside, it hangs in a cool, dry room in Italy — but what almost everyone buys is a pack of slices or a piece cut from a leg, and that is a large, thin, freshly handled surface that dries and oxidises in air. Take slices out ten or fifteen minutes before serving so they warm on the plate, and keep everything else cold.
en.fridge: Keep prosciutto at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, where it runs 2–3 months. Wrap a piece in paper rather than airtight plastic so it can go on losing a little moisture, and lay vacuum packs flat. Once a pack is opened the ham dries, browns and oxidises quickly, so re-wrap the slices tightly with their faces touching and eat them soon rather than counting on the full span. A puffy pack that has lost its vacuum goes back to the shop.
en.freezer: It keeps 1 month at −18 °C (0 °F) for best quality — a short window, and deliberately so. The fat is the whole point of prosciutto and it is the first thing a freezer damages: it oxidises, the texture turns waxy, and a thawed slice tastes of very little. Freeze slices interleaved with baking paper, bagged flat with the air pressed out, and use them in cooking. Frozen food stays safe indefinitely at −18 °C; the month is a quality limit.
en.thawing: Thaw in the fridge, still wrapped, and use the slices within a day or two. Never on the counter, and do not refreeze.
spoilage: A rancid, old-oil smell from the fat rather than a sweet, nutty one.
Slices gone grey-brown all through instead of deep pink with white fat.
Slime or a tacky film on opened slices.
Fuzzy green, grey or black mould on a cut face.
tips: Buy small packs; opened prosciutto dries out faster than you will eat it.
Stack slices face to face when re-wrapping so less surface meets the air.
Ask for it sliced onto paper rather than squashed into a tub.
Let it warm on the plate, never in the packet.

faq.q: How long does prosciutto keep in the fridge?
faq.a: 2–3 months at 4 °C (40 °F) or below. Once a pack is opened, eat it well within that — it dries and browns within days.
Yes, 1 month at −18 °C (0 °F), but it is a compromise: the fat oxidises and the slices thaw waxy. Use them cooked.

faq.q: Does prosciutto need to be refrigerated?
faq.a: Slices and cut pieces do. A whole uncut leg is a dry-cured product that hangs in a cool, dry room instead.

zh.name: 義式生火腿
zh.summary: Prosciutto 是義大利的風乾生火腿：整支豬後腿抹鹽後風乾一年以上，再切成薄如紙的片生食。放 4 °C 以下冷藏可放 2～3 個月，冷凍 1 個月。本站其他風乾整肌類的數字，多半就是以它為基準推出來的。
zh.pantry: 切片或真空包裝的生火腿是冷藏品，不是櫥櫃食品。整支腿是另一回事——又乾又鹹、外層還保護著內部，在義大利就是吊在陰涼乾燥的房間裡——但幾乎所有人買到的是切片包或從整腿上切下的一塊，那是一大片又薄又剛被經手過的表面，暴露在空氣裡會迅速變乾、氧化。上桌前十到十五分鐘把切片拿出來在盤子上回溫，其餘時間都放冷藏。
zh.fridge: 放 4 °C 以下，可放 2～3 個月。整塊用紙包而不要用塑膠密封，讓它還能慢慢散一點水；真空包請平放。包裝一旦拆開，火腿會很快變乾、轉褐、氧化，所以要把切片面對面緊緊重包並盡快吃完，不要傻傻地把整段時間算滿。真空跑掉、鼓起來的包裝請拿回店家。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下品質只有 1 個月，短得刻意。油脂正是生火腿的全部重點，而它也是冷凍庫最先傷害的東西：油脂氧化、口感變蠟，解凍後的切片幾乎沒什麼味道。要凍就用烘焙紙一片片隔開、平放裝袋壓出空氣，並把它用在需要加熱的料理。−18 °C 下安全性是無限期的，這一個月講的是品質。
zh.thawing: 維持包裝放冷藏解凍，切片一兩天內用完。不要放室溫，也不要再次冷凍。
spoilage: 油脂散發油耗、陳油味，而不是甘甜的堅果香。
切片整片轉灰褐，而不是深粉紅配白色油脂。
開封切片發黏、表面有黏膜。
切面長出綠、灰或黑色絨毛霉。
tips: 買小包裝；開封後的生火腿乾掉的速度比你吃的速度快。
重新包裝時把切片面對面疊好，接觸空氣的面積才小。
請店家切好放在紙上，不要硬塞進盒子壓扁。
要回溫請放盤子上，不要留在袋子裡回溫。

faq.q: 義式生火腿冷藏可以放多久？
faq.a: 4 °C 以下 2～3 個月。包裝開封後請遠早於這個期限吃完，它幾天內就會變乾轉褐。

faq.q: 義式生火腿可以冷凍嗎？
faq.a: 可以，−18 °C 下 1 個月，但那是妥協：油脂氧化、解凍後口感發蠟，建議拿去入菜。

faq.q: 義式生火腿需要冷藏嗎？
faq.a: 切片和切開的肉塊需要。完整未切的整支腿是風乾產品，該吊在陰涼乾燥的房間。
